title: Signal surface notation and sampling experiments
content:
Purpose:
A compact guide for a consistent signal surface notation (metrics + trace attributes) and a set of small, repeatable sampling experiments we can run to measure query-cost vs signal fidelity tradeoffs. This is an engineering-facing working doc — goal is to get consensus on naming, minimal attribute set, and a few experiments we can run during Q4 rollouts.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to tokenized text inference paths (hosted + dedicated) and embedding pipelines.
- Focus on operator-visible signals (what humans use during investigation) rather than heavy internal microbench metrics.
- We deliberately prefer compact attribute sets to keep cardinality low for dashboards and traces (tenant, route, model.family, sequence_bucket).

High-level requirements (operators):
- Fast triage: can answer "is this a capacity, model, or tenant problem" in <5 min for high severity incidents.
- Low-cost dashboards: per-minute panels should not blow query budget; prefer sampled traces and aggregated rollups for long tails.
- Reproducible investigation: traces and metrics must contain anchor IDs to correlate a trace to the raw request/prompt record (hashed id).

Signal surface notation proposal (naming + compact attributes):
- Metric naming convention: <component>.<noun>.<stat> e.g. edge.request.count, runtime.decode.p99, kv.prefetch.hit_rate
- Shortlist of required metric labels (tags): {tenant, route, model, family, seq_bucket} — these should be enumerated values where possible.
- Recommended trace span naming: service:operation e.g. frontend:parse, router:route_lookup, runtime:token_generate
- Trace attributes (minimal): span.trace_id, span.request_hash, tenant_id, route_id, model_name, seq_length, token_count, cold_kv (boolean), fallback_used (enum)
- Metric units & types: counters (requests, tokens), gauges (pool_util, kv_warmth), histograms (latency_ms)

Example metric schema (human-readable):
- edge.request.count (counter) — description: number of incoming requests accepted at edge. labels: tenant, route, client_version
- runtime.token.emitted (counter) — description: emitted tokens from the runtime. labels: tenant, model, family, seq_bucket
- runtime.kv.warmth (gauge) — 0..1 fraction, per-model-per-tenant estimate of KV cache hit probability
- runtime.generate.latency_ms (histogram) — per-request latency distribution, buckets: [0,5,10,25,50,100,250,500,1000,2500]

Trace annotation rules (to maintain low-cardinality while preserving fidelity):
- Only include high-cardinality values in traces (not metrics) but hashed: request_id_h = sha256(request_id)[:8] (trace attribute).
- Use seq_bucket for quantizing sequence_length into low/med/high bins to avoid cardinality explosion. Bins: 0-64, 65-512, 513-2048, 2049+
- For KV cache events: annotate spans that touch KV with kv.action=(read|prefetch|evict), kv.result=(hit|miss), kv.latency_ms.
- For fallback paths: trace attribute fallback_path=(none|model_variant|region_failover|graceful_degradation) and include fallback_score (0..1) if computed.

Dashboard and operator view notes:
- Two dashboard modes: Overview (1-2 panels per topic, ~30m granularity) and Investigator (multi-panel, per-tenant filters, 1m granularity, sample traces). Toggle should be visible and persist per-user.
- Recommended minimum Overview panels:
  - Global request rate (per-minute) + p50/p95 token generation latency
  - Dedicated capacity utilization by family (stacked)
  - KV warmth heatmap by model family and tenant weight tier
  - Failure surface (5xx, fallback rate) with top routes
- Investigator panels should include: top slow traces (sampled), request-level token counts, model variant rollouts mapped to latency and error slices, and a compact event timeline showing cache misses and fallbacks.
- Query budget controls: default dashboard mode uses computed rollups for >1h windows; raw tag-level panels only for investigator mode.

Sampling experiments (design + measurement targets):
We need quick experiments to pick safe defaults for trace sampling and metric rollups. Proposed experiments are small, reproducible A/B runs.
Experiment A: uniform trace sampling sweep
  - Sweep sample_rate = [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5]
  - Collect: fraction of incidents for which a sampled trace existed during a 7-day window, median investigable-latency (time-to-first-useful-span) for ops, and downstream cost (storage + query).
  - Success criteria: 95% of incidents (high-sev) have at least one trace at sample_rate 0.1, while query cost increases <25% vs baseline.
Experiment B: adaptive sampling anchored to anomalies
  - Implement cheap anomaly signal (edge.request.err_rate > baseline*3 OR runtime.generate.latency_ms.p99 > baseline*1.8) to flip sampling to 100% for affected route/tenant pair for 30m.
  - Measure detection lag, fraction of true incidents captured, and flash cost.
Experiment C: targeted tenant-weighted sampling
  - Keep global sample=0.02 but sample tiered tenants higher (enterprise=0.5, standard=0.05, free=0.01).
  - Measure: investigation completeness for enterprise incidents, cost per-incident, and fairness (are we missing regressions in free tier).

Instrumentation checklist for an experiment rollout:
- Add sample-rate flag behind feature flag (FF-obs-adaptive-sampling).
- Instrument quick rollup counters that report the number of traces ingested and storage bytes used per day.
- Ensure investigator dashboards can surface sampling rate per-tenant/route (label: observed_trace_sample_rate).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much of the request payload can we include in trace attributes (even hashed) before SRE/legal flags it? Need to coordinate with security/compliance.
- Do we want to encode model quantization/precision in metric labels? Pros: debugging regressions across quantization profiles. Cons: cardinality explosion when combined with model_version tags. Proposal: include quant_profile at family-level only (e.g. quant:8-bit, quant:fp16) not per-version.
- Retention tiers: which signals must be hot (30d), warm (90d), cold (365d)? Suggest: traces (30d), raw request logs (90d with redaction), per-tenant rollups (365d).

Immediate next steps / action items:
- Agree on final label set and seq buckets (owner: Miguel Ramos) — ticket RFC-OBS-1423 assigned.
- Run Experiment A & C in a small pilot (owner: Claire Nguyen) — aim: start pilot by 2025-11-10, results by 2025-11-24.
- Add sampling-rate visibility to investigator dashboard (owner: Benji Holt) — PR: telemetry#178
- Security review on trace attribute hashing policy (owner: Asha Patel) — add to security sync 2025-11-06.

Notes & references:
- Keep metric name short; prefer dots over underscores to group in dashboards.
- When in doubt, prefer a new label with enumerated values over freeform strings.
- For dashboards: default to pre-aggregated views and only enable tag-level breakdowns in Investigator mode.

Appendix: compact quick-reference (copyable):
Metric examples:
- edge.request.count | counter | labels: tenant, route, client_v | unit: count
- runtime.generate.latency_ms | histogram | labels: tenant, model.family, seq_bucket | unit: ms
Trace attributes (minimal):
- request_hash, tenant_id, route_id, model_name, seq_bucket, cold_kv, fallback_used

End of doc.
